summary: Steel-column tower built 1974-75 to replace a CCC-era lookout; the site had 1930s-40s summer staffing, a 1947 discontinuation, and is open to the public by dirt road.

facts.design: Steel-column enclosed tower with angle iron and steel rod cross bracing; the register says only five lookouts use this plan

access.note: Register says the site is open to the public, about 10 miles from paved road

visit.trail_note: About 10 miles from paved road per the register; Wikipedia describes the tower as accessible via dirt road. No trail or climbing notes found.

events.note: A 1920 district newsletter mentions a man stationed on Soldier Mountain as a lookout
Camp Big Springs CCC crew built the Soldier Mountain Road and the Soldier Mountain Fire Lookout Station in spring 1934
Newspaper notice says a man was employed at the lookout station for the summer by the Forest Service
October 1947 newspaper report says the Soldier Mountain and Bunch Grass lookouts were discontinued because of weather conditions; whether permanent is not stated
Current steel-column tower replaced a CCC-era lookout in 1974-75
National Geodetic Survey station description (1977) calls the enclosed metal lookout building about 20 feet high, from the concrete foundation to the top of the roof

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 5,454 ft for the lookout site; Wikipedia gives 5,531 ft for the mountain. The story reports the lookout figure and notes the higher mountain figure rather than merging them.

The register's 1974 date is for the current tower. The Redding article dates the first Soldier Mountain Fire Lookout Station to a 1934 CCC build, which the register also describes as the CCC-era lookout the tower replaced. Both are kept with their own dates.

notes_for_editor: The 1974 record date is correct for the current tower; the first station dates to a CCC build in 1934 (Redding) and a 1920 mention. Height 6.1 m comes from a 1977 NGS description of about 20 feet, converted; the register gives no height. The 1947 discontinuation is known only from a reprint of a Weekly Adin Argus item on the Forest Lookouts page; the original paper was not checked, and the closure may have been seasonal. Access is 'public' per the register, which is undated; no recent visit or staffing report was found. No fire events were found in the sources I read. Grokipedia says the station dates to the 1920s; it is an AI-generated page, so I did not use it. Photos are credited on the register (Ron Kemnow, 2008; Fred Johnson) but no image URLs were found, so no photo entries.
